tips.comment: Ardisia impressed on debut at Musselburgh, showing a nice turn of foot to squeeze through and win with a bit in hand. She’s open to plenty of improvement and sets the standard here on what she’s already shown. Should take plenty of beating.

Finished a good 3rd on debut despite clipping heels, stumbling, and then when making headway, was badly hampered. Still stayed on for 3rd, and with that run under his belt, should be thereabouts here.

Horse number 1 who did win on debut, will start as favourite , can be running well but there are some interesting newcomers. Supreme Dancer is well bred, good form in the pedigree mainly over further but for now , this distance looks ideal. Horses from this top trainer often run well first time out , stable jockey on board.

The 2yo made his debut two weeks ago and was not without support in the 17 runner, £21K novice stakes. In the mix a furlong out - maybe asked for his effort a little early - but wandered around a little late on and was outpaced, the jockey wasn’t hard on him. Something to build on and can be a player in this £3K novice stakes.

The Tutty yard were never known for their 2-year-olds, but last year they took this race. They have another well-bred, interesting newcomer this year, and with only the penalized Ardisia having shown any real form, I am hoping this horse can go close today.

Small eachway chance for this selection, the current favourite (horse number 1) could be overbet in this race , some interesting newcomers from decent trainers. This selection could run well at these good odds, good form in the pedigree, mainly over 1mile or so but for now, this horses starts off at an ideal distance. I think this race is slightly more open than what the betting market suggests, wouldn't surprise me to see the newcomers run well , but at the same time the current favourite could be too good for the opponents.

A 9 runner novice stakes, just one runner with experience - poor form. The selection is nicely bred and the trainer has good stats with his 2yo runners. The yard has sent out six runners in the last six days and has had two winners.

An open looking Novice Stakes race this, anything could happen. Small win tip for Go Victor who has an interesting french pedigree, some good form in the pedigree which suggests this horse could be running well on debut. Drawn well and a top jockey has been booked.

Although no show in the race, was not unfancied in the betting market on debut run in the Brocklesbury @ Doncaster over 5f. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, much better ground today will suit better, under used jockey up and very shrewd trainer who would not be really known for his 2yo's, is 25 percent with a Lsp of 16.65 in that sphere here last 5 seasons, making current 16/1 very good Ew value in the race.

It wouldn't surprise me to see some of the newcomers run well in this. Ice Cold Alex could at least outrun these odds, the selection has plenty of good form in the pedigree at 5f and 6f , starts off over an ideal distance of 5f today. The selection has one of the better draws so it wouldn't surprise me to see this horse thereabouts at the finish. Good jockey booked, very small eachway tip.

City Captain ran well when beaten 2 lengths off 55 at Chelmsford and looked like there’s still a bit more to come. The trip is a slight unknown but he’s fresh off a break and comes from an underbet yard (120 runs, 28 wins, 1.49 A/E, +87pts @ 72% ROI).
Has strong early pace and experience in higher-class races. Competitive time figures and ideal conditions today. Good draw and top jockey booking enhance his chance.

3yo gelding Ballsgrove Boy knocked at the door in his last three races with form figures of 223. He has dropped to a handy mark 7lbs below his opening hc mark and the step back in trip should suit. Will be in the mix.

This filly could well bounce back to form with a new trainer who puts the tongue tie and visor on and books Hollie Doyle for the ride. The mark of 60 is also a bonus since she won a maiden under almost identical trip and ground conditions where the subsequent runs of the 1st and 3rd easily make a case for this horse being rated 10lb+ higher than this mark. She was even pitched into Listed company after that (admittedly outclassed), but she could well win this off a mark of just 60.

Race 3 at Pontefract today is the Eventmasters.co.uk Handicap Hurdle (Class 4) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 3,822 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old gelding Mister Sky Blue from the Gemma Tutty yard, and will be ridden by Rowan Scott. After taking all into consideration, this son of River Boyne has the best overall form, which could result in the improvement needed for the win here. It should pay to follow.

Ardilly Breeze at a big 14/1 appeals here in this weak sprint. He opens his handicapping career off of a very good looking mark of just 54 and has shown enough in 2 recent all-weather races that he should be bang there today.

This lightly-raced maiden has had limited exposure on the track. Priced at 33/1, he finished 14 lengths behind the winner, Kilteel, in a nursery race at Newcastle. After a 6-month break, he returns with a favorable draw and is partnered with Ellie-May Croot, who has a 5lb claim. Croot is in good form, having secured one victory and placed twice from 5 races here. Therefore, an each-way bet at 33/1 seems like a worthwhile investment.

Likes a stiff track, and if you take out the ridiculously easy winner of its race last time, then Coverbridge was unlucky not to finish second - best of the rest. Has plenty of experience and has dropped in the weights.

Sanbona didn’t seem to get home over 8f at Redcar and has been out of sorts lately, but she’s back down to a more suitable trip here and could come on for last week’s run. First-time visor might sharpen her up and she’s turned out quickly, which could be a positive if she’s come out of it well. Worth taking a small each-way chance.

Looks a potential improver this season and should build on the promising 6th behind Teumessias Fox at Kempton LTO. 1 lb lower here and his impressive maiden win at Windsor was over this trip on quick ground.
A couple of good wins last year and made a promising return after an absence last time out. Finished 3rd in a big field at Doncaster. Runs off the same mark here and should be close.

Won on debut in a maiden at Leopardstown over 1m, up in trip today. Ran at group level as a 3 year old, although overall poor performance. First run for new yard after 299 day break was a poor 15/21 at Doncaster over 1m where he may have not enjoyed the straight track. Back at a left-handed track, still relatively unexposed with top jockey on board. Can go close.

I found it simple to put a line through the market principles in the feature at Pontefract this afternoon. M Botti rarely has one ready in the spring and his 1/11 record (A/E 0.29) with favourites in April proves this which puts Calumet up against it, meanwhile Qitaal has to overcome J Fanning’s 9% SR (A/E 0.43) on fancied 6yo’s. Ocean Of Dreams can’t be trusted given he’s raced just four times and didn’t look like the step up in trip will aid today after a poor reappearance run in the Spring Mile. FORCEFUL SPEED appeals to me with his 2/3 C&D record, 63% SR on similar going and reappearance run behind him; he beat just one rival home at Kempton over 11f last month but has shown previously that he needs that first outing to blow off the cobwebs. The son of New Bay is dropping back in trip today and a number of positive stats boost claims; most notable being Amo Racing’s 36% SR (A/E 1.68) at Pontefract, NB’s 31% SR (A/E 1.63) at the course too along with his 14% SR (A/E 1.4) with runners who finished 7th or worse LTO. 8/1each way taken.
Siempre Arturo had a great 2024 with five wins, with two of those being when first up after a break. He could improve again in this step up to C2 on the return.

Lightning Company ran better than the result suggests at Sedgefield, going a bit too hard early but still sticking on for third. The drop back in trip looks a smart move, and he’s clearly got enough ability to make an impact off this mark.
Worth a look each way off this bottom weight. Has won in Class 4 grade and has some useful previous form at Pontefract. The jockey's 5lb claim puts him in the picture at a big price.

Reel Her In didn’t land a blow over hurdles last time but was a consistent performer on the Flat last year and returns to a more suitable test here. The trip’s a slight question, but she’s tough and genuine, and with the yard going well in spring turf handicaps, she’s got a good chance if seeing it out.

Has been plying his trade over the winter months hurdling, and although he has not got his head in front in that sphere, there was nothing wrong at Huntingdon last month when runner-up over 19.5f. Switches back to the flat under Gina Mangan, who knows him well, and hopefully, he can win as he did at Catterick in October when last on the level.

She's The Duchess looked sharp on debut at Newcastle, traveling smoothly and knuckling down well to win by a neck. She drops back in trip here but has the pace for it. The trainer’s in form, and with that experience under her belt, she’s very much the one to beat.

Fifth of 12 at Newcastle in a handicap last time. Showed a little improvement on her three runs in maiden company for the previous yard, so is a very big price at 200-1. Dropped back into maidens now and also dropped slightly in trip. Has more experience than most of these and is entitled to come on for a recent outing. Can be played each-way at this price.

Reigning Profit is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Ruth Carr. He is a six-time winner with all wins coming over today's 5f. He is ground versatile and a two-time CD winner, one of which included a win in this race in 2023. He comes to hand this time of year with 3 out of 6 wins coming in April/May and looks well handicapped, being 1lb lower than his last win at Hamilton under today's jockey, James Sullivan. A major player!
Remains 4 lbs below last winning mark and ran well on reappearance at Doncaster when a strong 3rd. Has a good draw and fitness on side here.
The results haven't been a fair reflection on the ability of this horse. Dropping on OR again for today's race, the lowest rating this horse has been on. Also, with the jockey claiming 5 lbs.

Has been going very well on Aw of late, but is a C/D winner so just as effective on turf. Is better over this 5f than 6f, decent draw, good apprentice back up claiming 7lb and very shrewd training duo are 19 percent with a Lsp of 42.83 on his 4yo plus here last 5 seasons, making current 9/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Switch to AW not quite gone to plan, although performed well in a couple of races and was a bit rusty in return back to turf LTO when 5 of 7 at Nottingham yesterday. So, hoping she performs better being a quick returner.
At the top third of the handicap mark in this field and should welcome the dropped mark for tomorrow. So, he has a chance in what will be his course debut. Improvements required.

A Girl Named Ivy burned out a bit at Newcastle and hasn’t really proven herself over this trip, but she’s back at a track she likes and is a previous winner here. She might just be using this as a pipe-opener, but if things fall right and she settles early, there’s a small chance she sneaks into it at a price.

Better did win off a 55 back in October and did win off a 58 the year before when first up after a short break. I think this puts him in with an Each Way chance off today's 57 with PJ to help out while still only a 4-year-old.
Bit In Hand won maiden hurdle at Newcastle over 2m1f by 51 last time. Drying ground a plus; off a short break; feasible threat.

That One arrives at Hexham with solid recent form figures (4-5412), showing a progressive profile. The six-year-old has winning experience at the track and handles the 2m trip well. Trained by J. Walton and partnered with C. O’Farrell, this gelding combines consistency, course suitability, and race conditions in his favour.

Value bet in this. She is the best one in the race on the numbers. She is rated 104 against the favorite's 111, but is in receipt of 14 lb. On a strict line through her beating Willie Shake Hands on her penultimate start, she is only maybe a pound inferior to the favorite. So, on my book, she should at least beat the favorite comfortably if fit after a break.
Latest run was decent over this course and a huge step up from before. Overpriced here, and a similar performance will see him go close.
Kidman has not won yet and was a bit pants last time out in C3. But I am putting my faith in him being second up after wind surgery and getting back to C4.
Diamond Mix ran well when second at Newcastle. Then disappointing last time when tried over a longer distance. Back down in distance here and should go well.

Looks a very open-looking race with current market leader 'Kidman' worth taking on. My eye was drawn to this one after running a nice race at Carlisle (1m 7f 207yds) on good ground in a Class 2 Handicap Chase last month in what looked a much more competitive race than today's field when finishing 4th of 10 to 'Raffles Wonder', which wasn't a bad effort. With similar conditions today, it looks well worth a look off a 2lb lower mark.

Is a fair hurdler on his day and, having fallen at Carlisle back in October, was given a considerate ride next time at Ayr, probably to restore confidence, and finished a never nearer 5th over two miles. Was kept to that trip at Haydock but failed to get involved, albeit in a much tougher race. Appeared unsuited by the step up in trip next time at Newcastle but was better at this track last time, over hurdles. Goes chasing here from his hurdles mark and, having won a point, could reward each-way support with a clear round.

Not been showing that much of late, but interesting that some of their better runs have come here @ Hexham, where they were a C/D winner in 2023. Their chase rating has dropped to an attractive 84 here, normal pilot C. Nichol does prefer to ride another one in the race, but we have an able replacement in J. Hamilton and shrewd trainer best here with her chasers last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 solid Ew value in the race.

All 3 of his wins over fences have come at this track, and he will appreciate the faster ground having ran on soft last time out. He is now just 1lb above his last winning mark and relishes it here so should run well.

The model I run has Smart Decision to win this race comfortably (41% chance of winning) versus the next best horse, Bohemond Antioch (26%). Based on these results, it suggests the fair price for this horse is probably somewhere around 2.30. The price is incredibly short, so for me, it's more a question of value here. Worth noting, the jockey is also claiming 3 lbs.

This 4-year-old has been steadily advancing over hurdles, finishing strongly against tougher competition at Market Rasen a month ago. With Jessica Bedi's stable performing well and the jockey's 5lb claim likely to make a difference, the 25/1 odds offer fantastic value for an each-way bet.
Perhaps value for a little more last time out over course and distance and idled at the end. One of the few here in form and a good chance to go in again.
Back to form last time out when 3rd. Looks on a good handicap mark and now tried in first-time cheekpieces with conditions to suit.
This lad has good form here and has shown that the fire still burns in recent runs. A course and distance winner, he will need to overcome the jockey who at least takes 7 lbs off but is not a star.

Has dropped back to a mark of 97, just 3 lbs above his last winning mark. Also, 6 lbs lower than his ceiling handicap winning mark. He's 3 from 5 at this track. He's 3 from 4 over CD, so we know he goes well here. Admittedly, he ran a poor race over CD last time out. I'm not convinced he wants that softer ground, with his better form coming on better ground. His CD win back in November reads well. He beat Kelce comfortably. That horse has franked the form since, with form figures 1F21 since that run behind this fella, winning his latest run off a mark of 115. This is weaker than the races he's been contesting lately. If the fast ground can spark him back to life, we know this CD suits him to a tee.

Though Gibberwell has a 9lb penalty for winning over the course last time, adding to a course and distance victory in 2023, it could go close to gaining the hat-trick of course victories here today with luck in running and jumping under its 3lb claimer, Philip Armson.

This venue has seen all 6 of his career victories, but he is now well into his veteran years and hasn't quite recaptured his former strength this season. Still, his recent performances reveal that he remains capable of fighting for a good position. An each-way wager at 18/1 could be worthwhile for this battle-hardened athlete.

Thatsy is another that was not bad last time out when third and drops a couple of pounds for that. But more interestingly, is now second up after wind surgery, which is when I would expect to see more. EW 4P.

Recent form hasn't been too encouraging for this horse but he has ability and if he's on a good day, he'd be running well in this. It's interesting and a positive factor that horses from this yard have been running well just lately. The selection is on what does look like a competitive rating so has a chance on that, gets the cheekpieces back on today which may have a positive effect. Small eachway tip for Hold The Note.

Kickaftersix from the yard of shrewd Martin Todhunter has good jockey Henry Brooke onboard today. The horse last won at Hexham off a handicap mark of 79. It has been finally given a chance by the handicapper and is now rated 78. Each way 16/1... GET ON!
The horse loves this course, has been well supported in the market, is unexposed, and was only raised 1 lb, which looks handy with more improvement to come.

Comes into the race in good form after winning over course and distance in April and put the race to bed before entering the straight. Handicap mark has gone up, but jockey Ben Smith takes off a valuable 7lb.
Halpha Soleil was 2nd in his last two runs. LTO was in Cl4 contest .Today dropped in class has better chances to return to winning way under Brian Hughes.

Final Edgar can be running well in this fairly open looking race, he already has good form against some of these opponents , Final Edgar is now better treated than those he's met previously so it looks enough for him to get a lot closer today. Horses from this yard have generally been running well just lately so that is encouraging. The selection has good course form, trip and ground conditions ideal.

Larkfield Lusive is still a maiden after 18 starts, but he has run well in his last two starts. He was 3rd over 2 miles here last month and then 4th, beaten 7 lengths at Southwell two weeks later. He's down 1lb and on his lowest handicap, so looks like a good each way bet with 4 places on offer.

Cases to be made for quite a few of these, but I'll take a punt on this 11-year-old who finished 2nd over CD 20 days ago, beaten 2.5L. He arrives here having his 2nd run after a wind operation, which is usually a good aid to horses. The claimer taking a welcome 3lb off is also a plus point.

Reagrove Lord put in two good runs over further, one here in Dec and Jan, both soft, and shaped as if they stretched him a touch. Has gone well on good ground in pointing career, and the better ground today with a drop in trip can see the 7yo in better light. Looks capable enough of getting a place at least in this, after having a refresher run here a month ago. Rider claims his 5lb this time.

Yet to get his head in front under rules, but ran a better race at this track last time over a shorter trip. Sent for home too early under a vigorous ride. Should stay this far on breeding, and from a lower mark and a first-time tongue tie, could feature with a more well-judged ride.

A massive chance taken on this selection today but his form on sharp and undulating tracks could mean a good run may come out of nowhere. He won at Bangor in August off a 1lb lower mark, and he has performed well after a break previously but a huge chance is taken on him today.
Lunar Contact was pulled up in his last two races but will find the better going at Hexham more to his liking for his new connections in his first hunter chase.

Japetus is a clear favorite to win here according to the model I run. Good recent form of 2,1 over the same distance as today's race (2m) and looks open to further improvement. Limited quantitative data to go on here for these younger horses with limited experience, but the form and rating vote goes to Japetus.
This horse has traveled 285 miles from Berkshire. They wouldn't travel all those miles if they didn't see a potential to win.

Selection and hot favourite the only 2 with racecourse experience here and we have shown some promise in both runs to date. Pieces on first time today, top jockey booking and shrewd trainer is running @ 50 percent last 14 days, making current 7/1 the Ew play in the race.

Although Lady Jago has to give a stone or more to her three rivals, she does drop in grade here and has her top of the ground condition. Trainer Dan Skelton will be looking for another winner in his bid for the trainer's title, and she looks to have a great chance against some modest rivals.

Skelton is desperate for winners to beat Mullins to the championship, so we know all of his runners will be trying. This one has run well the last two times and was better than the result last time, kicking for home too soon and then blundering at the last. Comes here from the same mark.
Audacious Annie won when last out after a break. I would expect more now, second up and just up 3 lbs for that win. While there is no money in the bet, she will be a good multiplier in my lucky 15.

Won first time up last year, so goes well fresh. Big improver last year, winning 4 of last 5 starts, including over hurdles on penultimate start. Starts off the season from the same mark as when winning when last seen over fences last summer.
Ran to form, beaten 1 1/4 off 115 over 3m at Haydock last time where had run of race. Versatile ground-wise; contender.
I think Graham's form reads slightly better than his market rival, and I feel this race is between the two of them. A strong third was followed up by a good second, so the win is now on the cards.
Rock on Tommy looked in good condition when finishing second to a decent horse last time out. He has a couple of pounds in hand to the market leader, who also had a decent 2nd last time out.

Beaten a neck over course and distance in January. Disappointed in the subsequent two races, but they were both over right-handed tracks and further. The return to Warwick combined with the drop in trip could work, as could the first-time cheekpieces.
Big chance of following up here. His easy win last time was franked when the runner-up won next time out.

I like Mammies Boy in what looks like quite a strong race. Last run was on 9th May 2024. I think they've been waiting to run him again on good ground. As long as he is fit and ready to go, he will be competitive in this, as he hasn't run for 340 days. He was bumped, bullied, and didn't get a very clear run at all in the last furlong at Huntington and still won readily. Jonjo O'Neill Jr on board again.
Tarahumara is a 3-time winner who has been unsuccessful, though, in the last couple of races. Still, he is a quality player and should be closely watched on his preferably longer trip today.

Highly promising Frankel colt who is a half brother to severel winners and looked a good prospect himself where winning on his career debut when last seen at Yarmouth 182 days ago over the 7 furlong trip keeping on strongly inside the final furlong and won going away in good style now the manner he did that in was pretty smart for a first time out performance and Rogar Varian's inmate is certainly one to keep on side now stepping up in trip to the 1 mile 1 furlong trip here at Newmarket that being a positive move by his connections as this trip can unlock a whole new stage of improvement now as a 3yo jockey S De Sousa takes the ride on this good looking chestnut and can give this his best shot must be considered

Highly promising daughter of Night and Thunder who cost 440'000 gns as a yearling and most certainly looked worth that price tag when winning on her career debut by an impressive 8.5 lengths when last seen at Haydock 200 days ago now she may have had only the 3 opponents on the occasion however the manner she won in was very impressive traveling beautifully throughout and quickend right away to pull clear inside the final furlong in an impressive short space of time now on the back of such a performance William Haggas's inmate must be taken extremely seriously and strongly appeals as the type to move onto much better things now as 3yo steps up in trip for this return now tackling the 7 furlong trip that being a wise move by her connections as this trip can unlock a whole new level of improvement now returning to action as a 3yo jockey Tom Marquand takes the ride and can give Nardra a promising ride here at Newmarket merits serious consideration
